final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 (verified Lys at 119) is the catalytic lysine forming the internal aldimine with PLP; substituting Ala removes the covalent cofactor anchor and is mechanistically a complete null. AlphaMissense 0.987 and negligible Ala frequency among homologs agree.

G148 (verified Gly) lies in the conserved T-S-G-N-T PLP phosphate-binding loop, where a bulky positively charged Arg is sterically and electrostatically intolerable. Highest AlphaMissense score (0.996) with zero Arg observations across 85 aligned homologs.

G307 (verified Gly) mutated to Ser is the canonical pyridoxine-non-responsive homocystinuria allele with essentially undetectable residual activity due to misfolding of the catalytic core. AlphaMissense 0.828 supports pathogenicity, though its LOF acts partly through destabilization rather than direct active-site disruption.

stop_reason.detail: Converged Top-3 with independent mechanistic, evolutionary, and pathogenicity evidence; remaining tools address dimensions that would not reorder these candidates.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the Schiff base (internal aldimine) with the PLP cofactor; removing the ε-amino group abolishes catalysis while the fold is largely retained.
Verified K at 119; this is the PLP Schiff-base lysine, so substitution to Ala should abolish catalysis while leaving the fold intact.
K119 is the PLP Schiff-base lysine (verified K at 119), so removal of the covalent PLP anchor is mechanistically a complete null; AlphaMissense 0.987 and near-zero homolog frequency of Ala agree.
Classic severe, pyridoxine-nonresponsive CBS mutation in the catalytic core; steric addition at a tightly packed glycine disrupts active-site geometry.
Verified G307; classical severe, pyridoxine-non-responsive homocystinuria allele with essentially null activity.
AlphaMissense 0.828 (pathogenic) plus strong prior knowledge that G307S is the archetypal pyridoxine-non-responsive, essentially activity-null CBS allele.
Part of the conserved G256-T257-G258-G259-T260 PLP phosphate-binding loop; bulky Met should destroy cofactor anchoring and activity.
Verified T257 in the conserved GTGGT/catalytic region; a well-documented severe LOF allele.
AM 0.863 and Met frequency 0.012 support strong damage in the GTGGT catalytic loop, but it ranks just below the three mechanistically cleaner nulls.
Within the highly conserved TSGNTG PLP-binding motif; introducing a large charged residue is expected to block cofactor binding and catalysis.
Verified G148 inside the strictly conserved TSGNT PLP-binding loop; a bulky charged Arg there should be catastrophic for cofactor binding.
Highest AlphaMissense score (0.996) and Arg never observed at position 148 in 85 aligned homologs; G148 sits in the TSGNTG PLP-phosphate loop where a bulky charge is intolerable.
Well-documented severe pathogenic substitution causing misfolding/loss of catalytic activity in the catalytic domain.
Verified T191 in the catalytic core; a severe non-responsive allele, promoted above T257M/G148R.
AM 0.716 is the lowest among the pathogenic-class set, so it drops below T257M despite clinical severity reports.
Buried conserved arginine forming salt-bridge network near the active site; pathogenic and strongly destabilizing/inactivating.
Verified R125; conserved active-site-proximal arginine, reported as severe LOF.
AlphaMissense classifies it benign (0.153), inconsistent with a designed complete-LOF substitution.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense classifies it benign (0.153), inconsistent with a designed complete-LOF substitution.

history.rationale: Conserved arginine in the catalytic domain; reported severe loss-of-function variant disrupting subunit/active-site architecture.
Verified R336; buried salt-bridge arginine whose loss destabilizes the catalytic core, but activity loss may be partial/conformational.
AM class is ambiguous (0.423) and the MSA call has only 14% applicability, so evidence no longer supports a confident null.
Most common pathogenic CBS variant; buried hydrophobic-to-polar change destabilizes the catalytic core, though partially pyridoxine-responsive.
Verified I278, but this allele is the prototypical pyridoxine-responsive variant retaining measurable residual activity, so it is a weaker fit for complete abolition.
AM benign (0.159) and I278T is the canonical pyridoxine-responsive allele retaining measurable residual activity, so it fails the abolish-activity goal.

rejection.reason: AM benign (0.159) and I278T is the canonical pyridoxine-responsive allele retaining measurable residual activity, so it fails the abolish-activity goal.

history.rationale: His65 is one of the two axial ligands of the regulatory heme; loss of ligation impairs folding and lowers catalytic activity.
Verified H65 as a heme ligand, but heme-domain variants retain substantial catalytic activity and only alter regulation/stability.

rejection.reason: Verified H65 as a heme ligand, but heme-domain variants retain substantial catalytic activity and only alter regulation/stability.

history.rationale: Cys52 is the second heme axial ligand; substitution perturbs heme coordination and reduces enzyme activity/stability.
Verified C52 heme ligand; loss of heme perturbs folding/regulation but does not reliably abolish the PLP-dependent activity.

rejection.reason: Verified C52 heme ligand; loss of heme perturbs folding/regulation but does not reliably abolish the PLP-dependent activity.
